title: EXPOSING Indian Podcasts Spreading Pseudoscience
description:
From astrology podcasts to Instagram reels promising instant wealth, India’s digital space is overflowing with absurd pseudoscience. In this first episode of Let’s Not Get Fooled, Pale Blue Thoughts dives into the world of rubbish podcasters who give their mics to astrologers, numerologists, Vastu consultants, and self-proclaimed wealth gurus

These so-called “experts” claim you can attract money by writing on bay leaves with a green pen, pressing your ears 10 times a day, cleaning toilets for Shani Dev’s blessings, or even whispering to water to change its pH. Podcasters sit and nod while scamsters talk through their “Uranuses,” and gullible audiences cheer them on. The result? Millions of views, likes, and comments — proof that India’s obsession with pseudoscience is thriving.

But here’s the truth: astrology won’t fix your career, numerology won’t save your marriage, and Vastu won’t make you rich. These aren’t harmless quirks — they’re scams that waste money, spread ignorance, and exploit vulnerable people. Real wealth doesn’t come from bay leaves and chants; it comes from critical thinking, hard work, and science.

If you’ve searched for astrology scams India, numerology debunked, Vastu fraud, pseudoscience podcasts, Instagram scam reels, or astrology podcasters exposed, this video brings the rationalist perspective.

comments.text: If science can’t prove something now, it doesn’t mean it’s fake. Many big discoveries were doubted at first. For example, people thought germs couldn’t exist because they couldn’t see them, but later microscopes proved it. The idea of Earth’s plates moving (plate tectonics) was called crazy until evidence showed it’s true. Even black holes were once just theories, now they’re proven. Maybe tools or methods aren’t ready yet, so we should check new ideas carefully but not reject them too fast. Real science is about curiosity, testing, and staying open to new things.
